data.name: Kana
data.gender_notes: Kana is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Kana is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kinnari', which refers to a celestial being or 'Apsara' in Hindu mythology. The Kinnari is a beautiful and graceful creature, often depicted as a bird with the lower body of a woman. Kana signifies the inner beauty and grace that a woman embodies. It is a name that signifies motherhood, nurturing, and the ability to create and sustain life.
data.spiritual_meaning: Kana is a name that holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is believed that the name invokes the blessings of the divine mother, Saraswati, who is the goddess of knowledge, music, arts, wisdom, and learning. Kana is a name that represents the feminine divine and the power of creation and nurturing.
data.etymology: Kana belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of the Kinnara.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kana total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

He is best known for his involvement in the Mahabharata war, where he was a powerful ally of the Pandava brothers. historical_references.reference: Kana is also known as Karna, and he is considered one of the greatest warriors in Hindu mythology. He was born out of wedlock to Kunti, one of the Pandava mothers, and was raised by the charioteer Adhiratha. Karna was a loyal friend of the Kuru king Duryodhana and fought on his side during the Mahabharata war. Despite his loyalty, Karna ultimately fought on the side of righteousness and was killed by Arjuna, one of the Pandava brothers.
